simple.meaning: תְּלָאָה (tᵉlâʼâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “distress.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: תְּלָאָה (H8513) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Exodus 18:8, with occurrences in Exodus, Numbers, Nehemiah, Lamentations.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תְּלָאָה (H8513) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in תְּלָאָה (H8513) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: תְּלָאָה (tᵉlâʼâh) / H8513 is traced through Exodus 18:8, Numbers 20:14, Nehemiah 9:32, Lamentations 3:5 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H8513. telaah תְּלָאָה noun feminine weariness, hardship ; — ׳ת Exod 18:8 4 t.; of distress of Israel in Egypt Num 20:14 ; in wilderness Exod 18:8 (both J E); from Assyr., Babylonian, etc. Neh 9:32 ; compare Lam 3:5 (|| ראֹשׁ , gall); Mal 1:13 .

occurrences.englishText: Moses told his father-in-law all that Yahweh had done to Pharaoh and to the Egyptians for Israel’s sake, all the hardships that had come on them on the way, and how Yahweh delivered them.
Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom, saying:

Now therefore, our God, the great, the mighty, and the awesome God, who keeps covenant and loving kindness, don’t let all the travail seem little before you, that has come on us, on our kings, on our princes, on our priests, on our prophets, on our fathers, and on all your people, since the time of the kings of Assyria to this day.
